quote_zh: 倒入釜中进行碱解反应，反应过程微微放热，控制釜温为25℃，反应7h
arithmetic_check: Inputs as printed: sodium hydroxide 8.8 g at 48% stated as 0.105 mol, which gives 4.22 g of NaOH and 4.22/40.00 = 0.1056 mol, so it closes; methyl 2-chloro-3-(bromomethyl)-4-(methanesulfonyl)benzoate 34.8 g at 98% stated as 0.1 mol, which gives 34.10 g of ester and 34.10/341.60 (C10H10BrClO4S, from the drawn formula) = 0.0998 mol, so it closes. Base to ester is 1.05 to 1 by the printed moles, which the text never words as a ratio. No product mass, no product mole figure and no yield are stated for this step: the only product number is the in-process normalised content of 98.2%, so there is no mass balance to test and no discrepancy found. mass_balance_implausible and molar_mass_inconsistent are therefore not raised.
drawing_evidence: The scheme at line 277 (single arrow, step_id 1) supports this step: reactant COC(=O)c1ccc(S(C)(=O)=O)c(CBr)c1Cl is the named methyl ester atom for atom, the arrow condition text is NaOH, and the product CS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C(=O)[O-])c(Cl)c1CBr.[Na+] is the sodium benzoate the prose names in its in-process control. Drawing and prose agree on the alkali metal, on the base and on the surviving benzylic bromide, so no drawing_text_conflict arises. The only asymmetry is that the arrow carries no solvent while the prose charges 200 mL of tert-butanol, which is ordinary scheme abbreviation, not a disagreement, so reagent_written_not_drawn is not raised.

quote_zh: 室温下投入5.2g氢化钠(60％，0.13mol)，搅拌至溶解完全，经脱溶后得到三氟乙醇醇钠固体，密封备用
arithmetic_check: Inputs as printed: sodium hydride 5.2 g at 60% stated as 0.13 mol, which gives 3.12 g of NaH and 3.12/24.00 = 0.130 mol, closing exactly on the compound named. 2,2,2-Trifluoroethanol is charged by volume only, 50 mL, with no mass, density or mole figure, so its charge cannot be converted from the page alone and is not converted here; by volume it is a large excess over the hydride. No mass, mole figure or yield is stated for the isolated sodium 2,2,2-trifluoroethoxide, so there is no product-side arithmetic to test. Nothing fails: neither mass_balance_implausible nor molar_mass_inconsistent is raised.
drawing_evidence: No IMAGE_EXTRACT span depicts this transformation. The alkoxide appears only as a condition text, CF3CH2ONa, on the single arrow of the scheme at line 290, where it is a reagent of the etherification rather than a product of its own arrow. So this record rests on the prose of line 292 alone, and the drawings neither corroborate nor contradict it. That is also why the section carries two drawings for three annotated steps.

quote_zh: 将步骤(1)制备得到的2-氯-3-溴甲基-4-甲磺酰基苯甲酸钠盐(98.2％，0.1mol)分八次加入反应瓶中
arithmetic_check: Stated input: sodium 2-chloro-3-(bromomethyl)-4-(methanesulfonyl)benzoate at 98.2%, 0.1 mol, mass not printed. Stated output: 32.9 g of product at 98.7% by HPLC, and a two-step yield of 93.8% based on the methyl ester charged in step (1), which was also 0.1 mol. Check: 32.9 g at 98.7% is 32.47 g of 2-chloro-3-[(2,2,2-trifluoroethoxy)methyl]-4-(methanesulfonyl)benzoic acid, and 32.47/346.70 (C11H10ClF3O5S, from the drawn formula) = 0.0937 mol, which on the 0.1 mol basis is 93.7%. The printed 93.8% therefore closes to within 0.2 percentage points, inside the rounding of the assay and of the molecular weight. On 32.9 g uncorrected for assay the figure would be 94.9%, so the printed yield is consistent with the assay-corrected mass and not with the gross mass. Nothing fails, and mass_balance_implausible is not raised. The one thing a reader can get wrong here is the scope of the 93.8%: it spans steps (1) and (2), so it must not be scored as this step's yield.
drawing_evidence: The scheme at line 290 (single arrow, step_id 1) supports this step: the reactant CS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C(=O)[O][Na])c(Cl)c1CBr is the sodium benzoate of Step 1, drawn here with a covalent O-Na bond where line 277 drew the same salt as an ion pair, and the product CS(=O)(=O)c1ccc(C(=O)O)c(Cl)c1COCC(F)(F)F is the named free acid. The arrow carries two condition texts, CF3CH2ONa and HCl. Both are in the prose, and the drawing and prose agree on the sodium alkoxide, so no sodium versus potassium conflict exists in this section. The prose does place the HCl after the solvent strip, as an acidification of the aqueous residue to pH 2, while the drawing shows it on the same arrow as the substitution; that is scheme compression of a workup rather than a factual disagreement, so it is recorded in workup and noted, not flagged. THF, water and the eight-portion addition appear only in the prose.
